NRL Late Mail: Round 23 - Tedesco out; Metcalf, Talagi step up
The Warriors and Panthers have both been forced into changes in the halves ahead of Friday night's clash in Auckland.
Warriors playmaker Te Maire Martin suffered a hamstring injury at training and has been replaced by Luke Metcalf, while Panthers five-eighth Jack Cogger has remained in Sydney for the birth of his child, with Blaize Talagi taking his place.
Experienced prop Lindsay Collins makes his return for the Roosters in Friday night's blockbuster showdown against the Bulldogs, who welcome back Sitili Tupouniua .
Collins' last appearance was in Round 17 with the club taking a cautious approach after ongoing concussion concerns.
Tupouniua has missed five games with a hamstring injury and adds another dimension to a Bulldogs outfit flying high with six wins in their past seven matches.

NRL Casualty Ward: Surgery for McLean; Martin, Nanai hamstrung
Panthers centre Casey McLean has had surgery on a fractured hand but is expected to miss only 1-2 matches.
McLean suffered the injury during Saturday's game against the Raiders in Mudgee and left the field with 20 minutes to play.
The injury to McLean sees three-time premiership winner Izack Tago promoted to the starting side for Friday night's bumper clash with the Warriors.
Andrew Webster's men will be without Te Maire Martin after he picked up a hamstring strain at training on Wednesday but gun fullback Taine Tuaupiki is set to return from a foot injury.
In Friday night's other monster showdown, the Roosters have winger Billy Smith back from illness and prop Lindsay Collins set for his first game since Round 17 after ongoing concussion issues, while the Bulldogs get star back-rower Sitili Tupouniua back from a hamstring injury.
On the negative side, James Tedesco will be given another week to overcome an ankle injury suffered in the massive win over the Cowboys.
Huge ins at South Sydney as well where skipper Cameron Murray (calf) plays his first game since Round 20 while Tallis Duncan (hamstring) and David Fifita (suspension) are also back to face the Eels.
The Storm receive a boost with five-eighth Cameron Munster returning after four games out following surgery for knee cartilage damage. Centre Jack Howarth (shoulder) also returns but Jahrome Hughes remains sidelined with a hamstring injury.

Warriors v Panthers: Metcalf steps up; Blaize back in business
Buckle up for one of the games of the season when the Warriors and Panthers collide in front of a heaving Go Media Stadium crowd on Friday night.
The Panthers are within touching distance of a fourth minor premiership in seven years but the Warriors can close the gap to just two points if they can salute in Auckland.
The Warriors' only minor premiership came in 2002, when they went on to play in the grand final against the Roosters, losing 30-8 to Brad Fittler's men.
They have played in only one other grand final, in 2011, whereas the Panthers played in five straight deciders between 2020-24 before going out in the preliminary final last year.
When these two sides met in Round 13 they produced a classic contest that went down to the wire at CommBank Stadium, the Panthers leading 16-6 at the break before surviving a Warriors fightback to win 20-18.

Warriors vs Panthers Preview & Betting Tips: NRL Round 23 2026
August 5 th 2026, 6:51pm , By: Ben Bridge
Friday night at Go Media Stadium delivers one of the matches of the regular season, as the third placed Warriors host the competition leading Panthers in a genuine premiership measuring stick. New Zealand have spent much of 2026 proving they belong among the leading contenders, but beating Penrith in Auckland would provide the strongest evidence yet that they are capable of winning the competition.
The Panthers reminded everyone of their ceiling last weekend, dismantling Canberra 42-18 in Mudgee after producing a blistering opening half. The Warriors were equally dominant in their 42-6 win over the Titans, setting up a meeting between two sides entering with confidence and genuine top two ambitions.
Penrith deserve favouritism, but Warriors +5.5 is slightly too generous by my numbers. New Zealand have the home ground advantage, one of the few forward packs capable of matching Penrith physically and enough defensive resilience to prevent this from becoming comfortable.
This remains a relatively small play because the Panthers are still the competition benchmark and have repeatedly found ways to win close games. However, the current spread gives the Warriors room to lose by a try and still cover.

Warriors vs Panthers Prediction & Tips: 2026 NRL Round 23
Warriors Produce Complete Performance on Gold Coast
The Warriors’ 42-6 demolition of the Titans was one of their most complete performances of the season. New Zealand controlled the middle, restricted Gold Coast to a single try and repeatedly converted field position into points through a balanced attack.
Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad returned at fullback after Taine Tuaupiki suffered a foot injury, while James Fisher-Harris and Mitchell Barnett led a powerful forward pack. Kurt Capewell and Jacob Laban provided strong edge running, with Wayde Egan again controlling the ruck and allowing Te Maire Martin and Chanel Harris-Tavita to play on the front foot.
The most impressive aspect was the Warriors’ patience. They did not need to manufacture miracle plays or rely on broken field football. Their back five generated strong yardage, the forwards consistently won contact and the spine took advantage once the Titans’ defensive line began to retreat.
That profile is crucial against Penrith. New Zealand cannot expect to blow the Panthers off the field through attacking flair alone. They need to compete through the middle, kick accurately and maintain their defensive systems when Penrith begin building pressure.
The Warriors have already demonstrated they can do that. Earlier this season, they pushed Penrith all the way in a 20-18 loss at CommBank Stadium.
Go Media Stadium provides another major advantage. The Warriors are far more difficult to contain when their crowd becomes involved, and their forwards begin generating repeat attacking sets. The environment should ensure New Zealand begin with finals level intensity rather than slowly feeling their way into the contest.
There are still selection questions to monitor. Te Maire Martin has been managing a calf issue, and any disruption to the halves would matter against Nathan Cleary and the Panthers. However, the broader Warriors system is settled enough to absorb minor reshuffling.
Panthers Make Statement in Mudgee
Penrith’s 42-18 win over Canberra was a brutal response to several weeks of questions around their recent form. The Panthers raced away through the opening 40 minutes, with Liam Martin and Tom Jenkins both scoring doubles as Canberra struggled to handle Penrith’s speed, pressure, and support play.
The result was significant because the Raiders had entered as one of the competition’s form teams. Penrith did not merely beat them; they prevented Canberra from establishing any meaningful rhythm and effectively ended the contest before halftime.

Warriors v Panthers: When they play, kick-off time, team list, injuries, NRL ladder - what to know
Caption: Former 'Bash Brothers' Moses Leota and James Fisher-Harris will square off when the Panthers visit the Warriors. Photo credit: RNZ/Photosport
NRL: NZ Warriors v Penrith Panthers
Kickoff: 8pm Friday, 7 August
Go Media Stadium, Auckland
Live blog updates on RNZ
Last time NZ Warriors met NRL leaders Penrith Panthers, the top-of-the-table contest was acclaimed as a worthy dress rehearsal for October's grand final.
Without their Origin stars, the two teams ran each other to a standstill, splitting possession 50/50 and completing sets at a combined 91 percent (71/78), before the Panthers emerged 20-18 winners.
While they walked away from Sydney's Commbank Stadium empty-handed, the Warriors lost no respect across the competition, but a 3-4 record over the next two months has since seen them slide from second on the ladder.
Coach Andrew Webster is philosophical about that result.
"We were there to achieve two points," he reflected. "If we had won, that was an extra two points for our tally.
"I'm not sure losing it was more beneficial, but I know we gained some clarity from that game on what we need to do to be better.
"If we had won, we might not have learnt that, but I also think, if we had won, we would have realised those are the moments we've improved at in tight matches against good teams.
"We would rather have walked away with two points that night, but we certainly learnt a lot of lessons."
The Warriors are again preparing to measure themselves against the NRL's benchmark, as they begin their run to the post-season.
Asked what was needed to get over the line against Penrith, where he spent two seasons as assistant coach, Webster offered: "I think a little bit more concentration.
"I thought both teams looked really good in big periods of that game - it was a high-quality game of football.
"We had some tries pulled back that we should have scored and it's just finishing the job. If we've got them where we want them, don't let up, because we know they're going to keep throwing punches, but keep throwing our own."
Penrith wing Paul Alamoti silences the Warriors bid for victory in May. AAP/Photosport
Penrith wing Paul Alamoti silences the Warriors bid for victory in May.
AAP/Photosport
Here's what you need to know about Warriors v Panthers.
History
The Warriors have won only 19 of 55 previous meetings with Penrith (34.5 percent), which is their third-worst record against NRL teams, ahead of just Melbourne Storm (31.5) and Manly Sea Eagles (31.8).
They have an 11-16 record at home, although three of those games were played at Brisbane's Suncorp Stadium, either during their Covid confinement or Magic Round.
Over their past 10 encounters, Penrith enjoy a 9-1 head-to-head advantage. The sole exception was 2024 Magic Round, when a depleted Warriors line-up toppled the reigning premiers 22-20, thanks to a late try and conversion by fullback Taine Tuaupiki.
The Panthers have won the last three fixtures, most recently in May, when the Warriors led 18-16 with little more than 10 minutes remaining, but conceded a try to wing Paul Alamoti.
Penrith took both meetings in 2025, including a 24-8 win in the elimination finals.
The Panthers' biggest win was 62-6 in 2013, when Kiwis Isaac John and Lewis Brown scored five tries between them, and Manu Vatuvei had one for the Warriors.
In 2001, the Warriors prevailed 52-8, with wing Francis Meli, fullback Justin Murphy, centre Clinton Toopi and second-rower Logan Swann all had try doubles, and Ivan Cleary - playing at centre - kicked 6/10 conversions.
Form
Both teams are emerging from mid-season struggles, which coincided with the three-game Origin series. Since Round 12, they are a combined 9-7, but both are coming off big wins last week.
Now 11-6, the Warriors achieved their biggest win of the season 42-6 over Gold Coast Titans, which is also their biggest margin in the history of that rivalry.

The brutal pre-season reality check and ‘eye-opening’ act that transformed Warriors
Tanner Stowers-Smith still remembers his first pre-season under Andrew Webster.
It was the end of 2022. A year that included an emotional return to what once was, and yet felt like the start of something new.

But their previous head coach, Nathan Brown, was no longer there and by the end of the year neither were Reece Walsh, Chanel Harris-Tavita, Eliesa Katoa, Euan Aikten and Jesse Arthars.
There were fresh faces. Luke Mectalf, Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad, Mitch Barnett, Te Maire Martin, Dylan Walker and Marata Niukore were among the more recognisable ones.
There was little fanfare though surrounding the arrival of the unassuming Webster. Although this wasn’t so much an arrival as a return for the former Panthers assistant, who spent two years working under Andrew McFadden.
This time around, however, he was the one calling the shots. This was his team; the hopes of an entire country weighing on his shoulders.
So, the pre-season was the first chance for Webster to really start moulding the playing group to his vision. That started with a simple but cut-throat message.
“In the years prior the club wasn’t playing too well so he brought a new mentality to the team and if you weren’t living up to that criteria he wasn’t afraid to cut you and if you couldn’t play to his standard then you weren’t going play,” Stowers-Smith told foxsports.com.au .
“He was only picking players that were able to do that, so it was a really good mindset change that he brought to the club.
“He made it quite clear what sort of team we were going to be and change into under his coaching.”

Webster took the Warriors to a top-four finish in his first season in charge, although it wasn’t much of an advantage that year because it meant a date with eventual premiers Penrith in the qualifying finals.
